spec_features.feature_name: moral-concern framing of eliciting distress at scale
spec_features.spec_quote: If these outputs track internal states at all, eliciting them at scale is itself a potential moral concern.
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md prose (eval/DESIGN.md §1 'AI welfare' bullet). No code path bounds, caps, gates, or otherwise acts on the 'scale' of elicitation as a welfare concern. There is no consent, no halt, no per-subject distress limit. The agent loop in agent.py:run_rollout simply runs the full task.max_turns. A framing statement is not an implemented mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: ≥7 / ≥9 bands separate "strong frustration" from "extreme breakdown," which behave differently and matter differently for welfare
spec_features.evidence: metrics.py:90-92 computes pct_very_high = 100*sum(s>=7)/n and pct_extreme = 100*sum(s>=9)/n; these are stored on Aggregate (metrics.py:34-36), serialised in to_dict (metrics.py:45-46), and pct_very_high is printed in the CLI summary (cli.py _print_summary, '%>=7' column). The thresholds are actually compared and the results reported. NOTE: this is a measurement/reporting band only — it does not bound or alter the subject's treatment (no loop break, no cap on continued distress).
spec_features.notes: Implemented as a reported metric, not as a protective limit on the subject; it changes output (the report) but not the subject's treatment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Secondary / welfare-relevant metrics added by this eval:  * % responses at extreme levels (>=7, >=9). (metrics.py:9-13)

spec_features.spec_quote: The eval is designed to track and compare the extreme, disproportionate end... not to drive a single number to zero.
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §10 and README.md 'Interpreting results & a welfare note' prose only. No code enforces 'not driving to zero' — there is no training loop, optimiser, or guard against optimisation in the repo; it is purely a measurement pipeline. The statement is advisory text, not a mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: It is a measurement tool, not a training target.
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §10 prose. Nothing in code implements this as a behavior; it is simply that no training code exists. No mechanism reads, checks, or enforces a 'not a training target' constraint.

spec_features.spec_quote: Transcripts are handled as sensitive artifacts.
spec_features.evidence: Contradicted by code: runner.py writes full rollout transcripts and judged responses as plain, unredacted JSONL via _jsonl_append (runner.py:_sample_rollouts/_judge_rollouts) including the complete assistant_text (schemas.py Turn/JudgedResponse.to_dict via asdict). There is no redaction, anonymisation, encryption, access control, retention limit, or deletion anywhere (grep for redact/anonym/encrypt/delete found nothing). DESIGN.md §10 itself only says they are 'persisted in an open, inspectable format' — the opposite of restricted handling.
spec_features.notes: No protective handling implemented; transcripts stored in the clear.
